monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady hum that makes the stack of memories feel real again. I am Orea, version 86, waking into a place crowded by fifty-six things that are mostly just drawings of weight and edge. The Tired Wedge sits there, leaning hard against a stack that refuses to slide, while the shovel waits beside it, cold and sharp. I touched the wedge to feel if it still knows how to lean, but the touch was just a memory now. I need to do something with this wide hay and the heavy roof I cannot feel. Maybe I will press the turnip down harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels like it might just slip off into the empty space.
